guide:
The garden holds the work. Syntax: `attn seed <verb> --help`. The catalog is `attn seed --help`.

WRITING A BODY

A seed body is a prompt for the agent who will do the work. Write every body,
including the bodies of plot children, for a reader who has not seen this
conversation. Write it that way even when you plan to do the work yourself.

- Lead with the task and outcome: what to do and what done looks like.
- Give starting context: the problem, relevant paths or evidence, and constraints.
  Point to shared context and say what the reader needs from it.
- Define scope. Say what the work covers, what the tender may change, and what
  the tender must leave alone. Say which decisions need the user. Leave the seed's
  authorization out of the body. The authorization lists what the tender may do
  without asking and which actions wait for the user, and
  `attn delegate --authorization` sets the authorization from the user's words.
  Follow the
  `attn-workflow` skill's Delivery reference for repository delivery.
- Specify completion. Define the checks that verify the result on the seed, as
  CHECKS below describes, and cite each check in the body by id. Say where to
  leave the deliverable and what the report back contains.

Include an agreed design when there is one. Leave implementation choices open
where they are still for the tender to make. Scale the detail to the task. A few
sentences can be a complete prompt.

Keep the agreed task current in the body. Also write what a spike or
investigation established in the body, as findings below the task, because later
work builds on those findings. Put progress, other evidence, and handoffs in the
log. When the task changes, rewrite the body so it reads as the current task,
and use `--note` on the edit to record what changed.

EDITING A BODY

Export the body, edit the file with any tool, then submit it:

    attn seed export s-7k3f9m
    # edit s-7k3f9m.md and keep its first line
    attn seed edit s-7k3f9m -m - --note "what changed" < s-7k3f9m.md

The first line of the file is a stamp that names the seed and its body hash. If
another edit changed the body, export again and reapply your change. attn
refuses an empty body. Each edit saves an undoable body version and one log
entry, and `--note` adds your explanation to that entry.
Read the entries with `attn seed notes s-7k3f9m`. To restore the previous
version, run `attn seed rollback s-7k3f9m`. To restore a named version, run
`attn seed rollback s-7k3f9m 2`. Rollback saves a new version too.

WRITING A PLOT

A plot holds the shared plan. Its children are units of work, and a tender can
pick up each one on its own. A child can itself be a plot. Keep shared decisions
in the parent. In each child, state the child's own assignment and name each
parent section, sibling result, or artifact the child needs to read, with a
reason. Those references save repetition, but a delegation does not include
their text automatically.
A child's `show` lists the parent's headings and the item ids under each, and
`attn seed show <plot> --section <heading|D3>` reads one section. Name parent
sections by heading and decisions or findings by id.

Set `after` on a child only when the child needs a sibling's result. Otherwise
leave the children parallel. The children's states record progress, so the plan
needs no checklist.

Write the parent for an implementer who starts fresh and a user who reviews the
direction. Include the goal, the decisions the user might change, what spikes
and investigation established, the design, and how the children together
complete the goal. In the design, show ownership, interfaces, behavior, and
state, each as the smallest picture that explains it rather than prose alone.
The Planning reference in the `attn-workflow` skill gives the required form of
each part, with examples. Follow it when that skill is installed.

Example: move session search to the daemon while preserving its behavior.
The tender of the endpoint child records a contract that the app child needs
before the app child starts.

    attn seed plot -f plan.json

```json
{
  "title": "Search moves to the daemon",
  "body": "Move session search from the app to the daemon, so every client gets the same results from one ranking. Out of scope: changing what matches or how results rank.\n\n## Search behavior\nPreserve the current matching, ordering and keyboard behavior in app/src.\n\n## Decisions\nD1. Ranking moves to the daemon with matching, so the app renders results in the order it receives them. Open: whether search also covers ended sessions. The endpoint tender may decide, and nothing waits on it.\n\n## Tradeoffs accepted\nWe accept two search implementations between the two delivery steps, in exchange for each child landing on its own. The client index stays until the app uses daemon results.\n\n## Findings\nRead at a1b2c3d.\nF1. The app breaks match ties by recency (app/src/search/rank.ts). An experiment that ranked by match score alone reordered equal matches. The endpoint keeps recency as the tie-breaker. Dropping recency looks harmless and changes results.\n\n## Design\nOwnership:\n\n    internal/daemon/search.go          matches and orders sessions\n    internal/protocol/schema/main.tsp  SearchSessions message and its generated types\n    app/src/search/                    sends queries and renders results\n\nInterfaces:\n\n    SearchSessions{query_id, query} -> {query_id, sessions: [{id, title, rank}]}\n\nA new wire message needs an edit to main.tsp and a run of make generate-types. Commit the generated types and the protocol schema hash.\n\nBehavior:\n\n    app    -> daemon: SearchSessions{query_id, query}\n    daemon -> app:    ranked sessions for that query_id\n\nState:\n\n    latest query_id and keyboard selection (app, search store)\n      set by:      each query, and the keyboard moves the selection\n      on reply:    the app drops a reply for an older query_id\n      on failure:  the query and selection stay, and the results show the error until the next query\n      on restart:  starts empty and persists nothing\n    daemon: none added, and each query reads the live session set\n\n## Execution\nLand the endpoint child first, and record the contract on its seed. Land the app child afterwards, in its own delivery step.\n\n## Completion\nThe checks are on the seeds. Attach the recording for C2 to the app child, and cite it in that child's report.\n\n## Alternatives rejected\nFor D1: the daemon matches and the app keeps ranking. Each client would rank on its own, and removing per-client ranking is the point of this plot.",
  "checks": [
    {"id": "C3", "shared": true, "text": "The child is delivered through the repository's own delivery process, and that step's own checks pass. The report links the pull request or the landed commits."}
  ],
  "children": [
    {
      "title": "Daemon search endpoint",
      "body": "Add session search in internal/daemon. Read the parent plot's Search behavior, Decisions, Findings (F1) and Design sections. They give the SearchSessions contract, the ranking decision and its tie-break, and the protocol files. Trace the existing search in app/src to preserve its behavior. Follow repository protocol guidance. Test empty queries, matching, ordering and session changes (C1). Record the query and response contract on this seed for the app child. App integration belongs to that child.",
      "checks": [{"id": "C1", "text": "The endpoint's tests pass for empty queries, matching, ordering and session changes. Test run on this seed."}]
    },
    {
      "title": "App calls the endpoint",
      "body": "Route session search in app/src through the daemon, then remove the obsolete client index. Read the parent plot's Search behavior and Design sections and the Daemon search endpoint seed's recorded API contract. Preserve keyboard selection and prevent stale results when queries overlap. Verify search, rapid query changes and keyboard navigation in the running app (C2).",
      "checks": [{"id": "C2", "text": "In the running app, search, rapid query changes and keyboard navigation behave as before. Recording on this seed."}],
      "after": ["daemon-search-endpoint"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The plot's C3 is shared, so each child proves it with its own report. A
child's `after` names the siblings the child waits for, by slug or full title.
To plant the plot inside another plot, add `"part_of": "<plot>"`. To record the
seed whose work led to this plot, add `"discovered_from": "<seed>"`. Both take
an id or a slug. To read the payload from stdin, pass `-` instead of a file.

    attn seed plant "..." --part-of <plot>   add another child
    attn open <plot>                        read the rendered plan

Before you plant or delegate, read each body and its named references as a
fresh agent would. Can you tell what to do, where to start, which constraints
apply, and how to establish completion? Fill any gaps before you hand the work
off. A part you cannot fill means the work is not scoped yet. Read referenced
seed bodies with `attn seed show <id>`.

When an agreed decision changes, rewrite every part of the shared plan that
depends on that decision, and note why. Plant deferred work under the plot or
beside it so the work stays tracked.

CHECKS

A check is a numbered statement (C1) that the tender must prove with evidence.
The statement names that evidence. attn stores each check on the seed with its
latest report and verdict, so define checks as data, not as bullets in the body:
use `checks` in plot JSON, `--check "<statement>"` on plant, or
`attn seed check add <id> -m "<statement>"` later. `plant` and `add` number each
check with the next free id in the plot tree and print it. In plot JSON, you
write the ids yourself. In the body, cite each check by id, and keep there what
a check cannot store, such as an exemption or where long evidence goes. Ids are
unique across a plot tree and never reused. A removed check keeps its id, and
`attn seed check restore` brings it back.

On a plot, `"shared": true` puts a check on every leaf seed below the plot,
meaning every seed with no children. The tender of each leaf proves the check
with that leaf's own report, and the plot shows how many are confirmed. Put a
check that only one child needs on that child. A plot check without `shared` is the plot's own.

    attn seed check report <id> <C#> -m "<summary line>" --evidence <file|artifact|url> --commit <rev>
    attn seed check confirm <id> <C#> [-m "<how you verified it>"]
    attn seed check reject <id> <C#> -m "<what would prove it>"

If you do the work, report each check with its own `attn seed check report`
call as soon as you prove it. The first line of `-m` is the summary line that
`attn seed show` prints. The summary line is at most 400 characters, and attn
refuses a longer one. The lines after it are detail, and attn keeps them in the
report's check note. `--evidence` takes a local file, which attn copies onto the
seed, an artifact already on the seed, or an http(s) URL. Reporting again
creates a new report. The new report replaces the last report and clears the
verdict. Citing a changed file under the same name
replaces the old file. `attn seed show` marks a report whose cited file changed
after the report, until the next report. For a check that does not apply, report
why and cite what shows it.

If you judge the work, confirm or reject each report. You may also confirm a
check that has no report when you verified it yourself. Checks never block a
move, but harvest names the ones still open or rejected.

WHAT DONE IS, BY DELIVERABLE

Adapt the assignment and its completion check to the work:

    code       The requested behavior exists and required verification passes.
               Give the starting points, constraints and any agreed design.
    bug fix    The cause is found and fixed, with a regression test. Give the
               symptom, reproduction and known evidence. Leave an unproven fix open.
    research   A sourced answer supports a decision. State the question, the
               decision it informs and the expected report.
    docs       The intended audience can understand or act on the result.
               Name what it must explain and which existing text it replaces.
    refactor   The named code issue is gone and behavior is preserved.
               Identify the issue and the checks that establish preservation.
    spike      The result answers a design question or lets the user judge the
               experience. State the question the spike should answer. Write
               the findings in the plan the spike informs, or below the task in
               the spike's own body until a plan exists. The spike's code is
               disposable unless the user decides to keep it. A prototype is a
               spike whose result is options for the user to choose between.

The garden instructions explain how to repeat a move, why you replant a seed
before you change how it closed (harvested or withered), and why a plot closes
only after its direct children. They also explain
`attn seed harvest <id> --when-merged`, which harvests the seed when its pull
request merges. Use it only when the merge is the last step.

ARTIFACTS

Bring a local file into durable seed ownership with an explicit Move or Copy:

    attn seed attach <id> --path <file> --move
    attn seed attach <id> --path <file> --copy
    attn seed detach <id> --path <filename> --to <destination>

Prefer Move, because the seed then owns the one canonical editable
file. Copy leaves the source alone. attn refuses Move for a tracked Git file, so use Copy. If you
attach a name the seed already has, attn replaces that file, whether the new
file comes from the same source or another one, and does not keep the old
bytes. Re-attaching an unchanged file changes nothing. Detach never overwrites
its destination. The seed keeps its owned file after the source worktree goes
away, the session ends, or the seed closes.
Every visible regular file directly under the seed's artifact directory belongs
to the seed, so ordinary filesystem edits and renames appear in the Garden.

Repository, Notebook and URL documents remain linked where they already live:

    attn seed attach <id> --path <file.md> --repo <repository>
    attn seed attach <id> --notebook <document-id>
    attn seed attach <id> --url <url>
    attn seed detach <id> --path <file.md> --reference

The Garden labels old path associations as linked files. To bring a linked file
into seed ownership, use the Garden's Move or Copy action on that file. The
link disappears only after the transfer succeeds.

HANDOFFS AND STEERING

    attn seed note <id> -m "…" --handoff   for the next tender. attn seed tend prints the
                                            handoff on the claim. attn seed show lists the
                                            handoff among the newest entries, or points at it
                                            when the handoff is older
    attn agent msg <seed-id> "…"            reaches the seed's current or next tender,
                                            and waits when none is reachable
    attn seed show <id> --since <N>         only what was saved after bookmark N.
                                            show and notes print the bookmark to use next

Leave a handoff whenever you park a seed, or stop partway through the work and
do not intend to continue. State the outcome, the evidence, and the next action.
Put long reasoning in an attached artifact, not in the note. Noting does not end
your session, so keep working unless you are blocked or done.
help:
usage: attn seed <command>

A seed is the unit of work: one document, one short id, one slug made of the
title's key words, planted in the garden. Commands take the id or the slug; a
slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.
Anything worth handing off, parking, or attributing is a seed.
Use attn seed <command> --help for one command's syntax and flags.

commands:
  plant "<title>" [-m <body>] [--part-of <plot>] [--discovered-from <seed>] [--check "[C#=]<statement>"]... [flags]
        plant a seed and print its id, slug and title. -m takes markdown, or - to read stdin —
        if the seed gains children, that body is the plot's plan. --part-of
        plants it under a plot. --check defines what the seed must prove;
        attn numbers it unless C#= names the id, and prints each id.
        Lists up to 3 similar open seeds in your profile, leaving out that plot.
        Planting always proceeds. If one is the same work, wither the new seed.
        --json prints the new seed alone.

  plot [-f <path>] [--json]
        plant a whole plot in one move from a JSON payload (-f, or stdin):
        {"title": …, "body": …, "checks": [{"id": "C5", "text": …, "shared": true}],
        "part_of": "<plot>", "discovered_from": "<seed>",
        "children": [{"title": …, "body": …, "checks": […],
        "after": ["<sibling step slug>"]}]}. Children are parallel by
        default; after names the siblings a child waits for. part_of and
        discovered_from are optional and take an id or a slug. A shared check is
        proven by every child. The plot, its children and their edges commit
        together. Prints the plot's id and each child's id and step slug, then
        up to 3 similar open seeds across all planted titles, each naming the
        new seed it resembles. Planting always proceeds; wither a new seed if a
        suggestion is the same work.
        --json prints the whole result, including similar seeds.

  ls [--plot <plot> | --stale [--window <duration>]] [--flat] [--json]
        the garden, newest first, with children nested under their plot.
        --flat prints one list. --plot lists every child of one plot, oldest
        first, harvested and withered included. --stale narrows to open seeds
        whose log has not moved for the window (default 7d) — a query for
        your judgment, never a reaper.

  search <words> [--limit <n>] [--json]
        find seeds by words across your profile's garden, harvested and withered
        included: titles, bodies and log entries. Words match as stemmed prefixes;
        identifier parts match too. Seeds carrying some words also appear.
        Ranks by title coverage, word coverage, relevance and recency, with a boost
        for open seeds. Prints status, last active and an original matching line.
        Shows the best 10 by default; --limit asks for more, up to 1000.
        Search before you plant, so a duplicate is found instead of created.

  ready [--plot <plot> | --all] [--json]
        what you can tend right now, oldest first: nothing open blocks it,
        nobody is holding it, and it is not a plot — a plot's work is its
        children. With no flags the scope is your profile's garden — unless this
        session was dispatched at a plot, and then that plot; --all steps back
        out to the garden.

  link <a> <blocks|part-of|discovered-from> <b> [--json]
        relate two seeds. "a blocks b" keeps b out of ready until a closes;
        "a part-of b" puts a under b; b is then a plot. "a discovered-from b"
        records where work came from without ordering it. A structural cycle
        is refused, naming both seeds and the edge to remove.

  unlink <a> <blocks|part-of|discovered-from> <b> [--json]
        remove the edge. Every link has one.

  show <id> [--since <bookmark> | --section <heading|id>] [--json]
        one seed, news first: its state, who tends it and a bookmark; the newest
        entries on its log, and where the freshest handoff is when it is older
        than those; every edge that touches it, with seeds discovered from it
        folded to a count and the open ones; the outline of the plot it is part
        of; a plot's open children as a board, each with what it waits for, its
        checks and its newest entry, closed children folded into one line;
        checks and artifacts; the body last.
        --since <bookmark> prints only the log entries saved after it, on this
        seed and every seed below it, newest first and labeled by seed, then a
        new bookmark. --section prints one part of the body: the section under a
        heading, or every item that starts with an id like D3.

  review <start|show|cancel|retry|keep>
        start an advisory Garden review, inspect its progressive results,
        cancel unfinished classification, retry one failed or changed item, or keep
        one seed growing and review it again after seven quiet days.
        The review never changes a seed's state.

  review start [--json]
        Start an advisory Garden review. The review never changes a seed's state.

  review show [<review-id>] [--json]
        Inspect the review and its progressive results. With no id, show the latest review.

  review cancel <review-id> [--json]
        Cancel unfinished classification.

  review retry <review-id> <seed-id> [--json]
        Retry one failed or changed review item.

  review keep <review-id> <seed-id> [--json]
        Keep a seed growing and review it again after seven quiet days.

  watch <id> [--json]
        watch this seed and its descendants. Delegation starts the same watch.
        Tending a plot already covers its descendants until the claim ends.
        unwatch removes this seed's subscription; separate child or ancestor
        watches remain. show names the subscriptions that still cover a seed.

  unwatch <id> [--json]
        Remove this seed's subscription. Separate child or ancestor watches remain.
        show names the subscriptions that still cover a seed.

  edit <id> -m - [--note "<what changed>"] [--json]
        save an exported body after editing the file with any tool. Keep the first
        stamp line. If the body changed since export, export again and reapply.
        Empty bodies are refused. Each edit saves a numbered version and a log entry;
        --note adds what changed to that entry.

  rollback <id> [<version>] [--json]
        restore the body before the newest version, or the numbered version.
        The restored body becomes a new version, so rollback can itself be rolled back.
        Edit entries in notes show the versions and size changes.

  authorization <id> ["<words>" | --clear] [--json]
        set, clear or print the user's words for this task: what agents may do
        without asking and where they stop. Set only words the user gave you.
        Delegation openings deliver them. When someone other than the seed's
        tender changes them, attn types the change into the tender's conversation
        as the user's message, waiting while the tender needs approval. With
        neither words nor --clear, prints them and the state of the last typed update.
        Who may change them follows seed moves: the tender, sessions above it in
        the delegation chain, and the profile's chief; anyone in the profile while
        nobody holds the seed.

  send-to-chief <id> [-m "<optional guidance>"] [--json]
        give this seed to the Chief to decide its next working context. The
        saved folder, branch and placement problem are recorded automatically;
        -m adds an exception such as a special branch or directory.

  tend <id> [-m "<why>"] [--for <name>] [--force] [--json]
        claim the seed and start growing it. The freshest handoff prints on
        the claim, so picking a seed up primes you. Tending your own claim again
        changes nothing and rings nobody. --for <name> assigns the seed to a crew
        member instead; the user never claims a seed, so a tend from outside an attn
        session needs it.
        A claim yields to its tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, or
        the profile's chief. A crew member's claim lasts across the member's sessions;
        a session's claim holds while the session is live and returns when it resumes.
        The log records standing and forced moves and whose claim ended. Everyone else
        needs --force. A call without a live session has no standing.

  park <id> [-m "<where you left it>"] [--force] [--json]
        pause the seed deliberately — it is parked and lets go of its
        tender. An optional comment lands on the log in the same move. Tending
        it again picks it back up. Parking it again keeps the state and adds
        only the optional comment. Moves print who they rang.
        A claim yields to its tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, or
        the profile's chief. A crew member's claim lasts across the member's sessions;
        a session's claim holds while the session is live and returns when it resumes.
        The log records standing and forced moves and whose claim ended. Everyone else
        needs --force. A call without a live session has no standing.

  harvest <id> [-m "<what got done>"] [--when-merged [<pr-url>] [--clear]] [--force] [--json]
        close the seed as done, with a required -m reason. Repeating a harvest
        succeeds with the earlier reason; a different reason goes on its log.
        A withered seed must be replanted first. A plot refuses while any direct
        child is open, including with --force or --when-merged; replant hands it
        back if your part is done. Closing the last child leaves a ringing note
        on the plot, names it here and keeps the plot's state. Moves print who they rang.
        --when-merged releases your claim and harvests the seed with your -m
        reason when the pull request merges. Without -m it uses "PR #N merged:
        <title>". This command merges nothing. Use it only when the merge is
        the last step. With no url it takes this session's single open pull
        request; --when-merged --clear takes the arming back.
        A claim yields to its tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, or
        the profile's chief. A crew member's claim lasts across the member's sessions;
        a session's claim holds while the session is live and returns when it resumes.
        The log records standing and forced moves and whose claim ended. Everyone else
        needs --force. A call without a live session has no standing.

  wither <id> [-m "<why>"] [--force] [--json]
        close the seed as abandoned. Nobody is picking this up. Repeating it
        keeps the earlier reason and adds a different reason to the log. A
        harvested seed must be replanted first. A plot refuses while any direct
        child is open, even with --force; replant hands it back if your part is done.
        Closing its last child leaves a ringing note on the plot and names it here.
        Moves print who they rang.
        A claim yields to its tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, or
        the profile's chief. A crew member's claim lasts across the member's sessions;
        a session's claim holds while the session is live and returns when it resumes.
        The log records standing and forced moves and whose claim ended. Everyone else
        needs --force. A call without a live session has no standing.

  replant <id> [-m "<why>"] [--force] [--json]
        put the seed back in the pool — planted, unclaimed, ready for whoever
        is free. Reopens a closed seed, takes a parked one off hold, and hands back
        one being grown. Replanting an already planted seed changes nothing
        and rings nobody. Moves print who they rang.
        A claim yields to its tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, or
        the profile's chief. A crew member's claim lasts across the member's sessions;
        a session's claim holds while the session is live and returns when it resumes.
        The log records standing and forced moves and whose claim ended. Everyone else
        needs --force. A call without a live session has no standing.

  note <id> -m "<what happened>" [--handoff] [--ring] [--json]
        append to the seed's log — what happened and what you learned, for
        whoever tends it next. - reads stdin. --handoff addresses it to your
        successor on this seed: tend prints the freshest one on the claim, so
        it is read before any work, and show points at it once newer entries
        bury it.
        --ring tells current and covering plot tenders and watchers to look;
        ordinary notes stay quiet.

  check <add|edit|remove|restore|report|confirm|reject|uncheck|reopen>
        Define, report, or judge what a seed must prove. Each move has its own --help.
        Checks never block a move. harvest lists the checks still open or rejected.

  check add <id> [<C#>] -m "<statement>" [--shared]
        Define a statement the seed must prove and print its id, which the body
        cites. attn picks the next free id in the plot tree; <C#> names one
        instead. On a plot, --shared makes every seed below it prove the check
        with its own report. Removed ids are never reused.

  check edit <id> <C#> -m "<statement>"
        Replace the check's statement.

  check remove <id> <C#>
        Remove a check. Its id stays reserved.

  check restore <id> <C#>
        Bring a removed check back with its result.

  check report <id> <C#> -m "<summary line>[\n\n<detail>]" [--evidence <file|artifact|url>]... [--commit <rev>]
        Record the proof for a check in one call. The first line of -m is the

To change a seed's body, export the body, edit the file, and submit it with `attn seed edit`. `attn seed guide` gives the steps and explains how to undo an edit.

Keeping up:

attn writes an entry in the seed's log for every change: notes, handoffs, moves, links, edits, checks, attachments, and answers. `show` prints a bookmark under the header, and a `notes` or `--since` read ends with a bookmark. Keep the bookmark from your last read, and read the entries since that bookmark instead of reading the whole seed again.

When attn sends an update notification, run the read that the notification names. Reading acknowledges the update and keeps you aware. It does not authorize or require you to act on the update. Act on an update, or interrupt the user, only when the update genuinely requires your action or the user's attention.

    attn seed show <id> --since <N>  only the entries saved after bookmark N, on the seed and every seed below it
    attn seed notes <id>             the whole log, newest first. It takes `--since <N>`, and `--kind <kind>` for one kind
                                     of entry, such as handoff or answer
    attn seed watch <id>             watch this seed and its descendants. `unwatch` removes the subscription
    attn seed attach <id> --path <file> (--move | --copy)    bring a local file into durable seed ownership, replacing a file of the same name. Prefer Move
    attn seed detach <id> --path <filename> --to <destination>    move an owned file back out without overwriting
    attn seed attach <id> --path <file> --repo <repo> | --notebook <doc-id> | --url <url>    keep a link to a document elsewhere
    attn seed export <id> [--out <path>]    the raw body with its first-line stamp

When you tend a plot, you receive updates from every seed under it, without a watch. When you end the claim, that coverage stops, and attn withdraws unread updates unless a watch still covers them. A new delegation starts an ordinary watch on its seed. `unwatch` removes that subscription, but separate child or ancestor watches remain. `show` and `unwatch` name the subscriptions that still cover a seed and say how to remove them. `watch` restores a subscription. A new delegation starts the watch again, but a restart or recovery does not. A crew member's watch belongs to the member and lasts across the member's sessions.

Use `attn agent msg` for attn-managed sessions. Use Claude's SendMessage only for follow-ups to the native subagents this session spawned.

Run `attn session rename "<a few words>" [--session <id>]` to rename a session, yours by default, when its main work no longer matches the name it started with.
